description: LIKELY ROOT CAUSE FOUND for B28 NAE-28 cluster (AHU-3/4/6/7/11): B28 Secondary Chilled Water Supply Temp alarmed HIGH 46.6-47.6F on 7/3-7/4, sourced from JL-BLDG17-NAE20 Secondary Pump 1-2 (physically B17 Rm 1010). B28 has no local chiller plant - fed by this B17 secondary system. Same B17/NAE-20 location has cooling tower level alarms on Towers 12, 15, 16 (7/3-7/4) and DA tank near overflow (40-42in). Points to a capacity-constrained chiller plant at B17 as the actual source, not a B28-side fault. B28 AHU-7 hit 90.0F on 7/4 (worse than the 68.4F we tracked 7/2) - cluster kept climbing while unmonitored. NEXT: check B17 NAE-20 chillers 12/15/16 and secondary pump 1-2 status directly; this supersedes the earlier CWP-15 guess for B28 specifically (CWP-15 may still be relevant elsewhere, not confirmed which system it serves).

RELAPSE: improved to 68.4F on our 10:30 AM 7/2 check, then spiked back to 85.7F at 1:07 PM same day (alarm log). Whatever fixed it that morning did not hold - unit is unstable/cycling, not resolved. Needs re-check, not closed out.

UNRESOLVED 5-DAY PATTERN: 80.1F overnight DAT alarm recurring 7/1, 7/2, 7/3, 7/4, 7/5 - same value, same overnight window each time. Flagged days ago to check NAE-27 OAT sensor, never actually checked. Still happening nightly.

NEW THREAD: broad zone-temp problem across B51 SNE-03 - a dozen+ rooms (2600, 2610A, 2630, 2650, 2652, 2654, 2710, 2720, 2930A, 2950D, 2950E) hitting 78-91F daily/recurring. Rm 2600 specifically spiking 90-91F repeatedly. AHU-level discharge temps in this building have looked fine in DAT sweeps (AHU-3A/3B ~55F, PIV units cold). Mismatch suggests a DOWNSTREAM problem - VAV boxes, reheat, or zone dampers - not the AHU coils. Separate from the plant-capacity story, needs its own investigation.

outcome: Readings swung wildly -171F to +72F repeatedly on 7/6 04:20-04:57 AM (alternating Unreliable/Low Alarm), settled to a normal 71-73F by 05:18 AM. Sensor is failing intermittently - needs replacement, not just a reset. Object: 1055066CGE Rm 1345, JL-BLDG55-SNE01.

description: CORRECTION - real root cause found: this is a DX unit, not chilled-water/OAT-lockout. Cross-referenced Compressor Status 2 alarm against the DAT timeline on 7/2: Compressor 2 went Off at 12:53:53 PM, DAT alarmed 85.7F at 1:07:23 PM (13 min lag - consistent with losing cooling capacity), DAT recovered to 77.9F by 1:25:38 PM, Compressor 2 came back On at 1:35:22 PM. The earlier AM improvement (85.7->68.4) and the PM relapse were the SAME compressor cycling off and on, not an OAT sensor issue and not an unstable override. Drop the OAT-lockout theory for this unit entirely. NEXT: physical check on Compressor 2 - contactor, high/low pressure safety switch, refrigerant charge, condenser fan/airflow. Object: 1006000FAC AHU-1, JL-BLDG06-SNE11.

ESCALATED to critical tier: recurring DAT alarms 7/2-7/4, climbing 69.3F -> 72.6F (+15-17F over 55F SP). Same cluster (JL-BLDG29-SNE31/FCB.31A012FEC Annex 5 PIV Control) also threw Discharge Air Humidity high alarm at 85.8%RH. Multi-day, not self-resolving. Was tracked as high tier (+4-5F) from the 7/1-7/2 sweep - needs re-sweep and physical check, likely same plant-capacity or valve issue pattern as B28.

POSSIBLE LINK: 4 rooms (Staff Office 2915, Classroom/Fitness 2920, Womens Lckrm 2930, Mens Lckrm 2925) all hit 84.5-85.4F on 7/4-7/5. Same day (7/4 2:12-3:57 PM), B57 AHU-3 (04A015UN, N2-1 trunk SNE-04) threw a VFD Speed Command Failure, dropped to 0%, only recovered to 22%. Check whether AHU-3 serves the wellness area - if so this VFD issue is the likely cause of all 4 room alarms, not 4 separate faults.

Recurring dehumidification problem: Discharge Air Humidity alarmed 85-86%RH on both 7/2 and 7/4 (2 days apart), same controller (1055026CGE Rm 3945) also threw a Reheat Effort alarm on 7/2. Pattern suggests reheat/dehumid control is not keeping up, not a one-off blip.

MAJOR RECOVERY 7/6 12:00 sweep: 1 critical / 3 high, down from 9 critical / 17 high on 7/2. Resolved: B28 AHU-1/2/3/4/7 (NAE-28 cluster), B28 AHU-11, B29 AHU-1/2 + Annex 5 PIV, B33 AHU-1/2, B53 AHU-2 (was stuck +6-7F for days), B55 AHU-3 (strainer job worked), B64 AHU-1/2 (resolved without the deferred override), B1 building (AHU-16/Dirty/AHU-3), B6 AHU-1 (compressor stable). This is consistent with the B17/NAE-20 secondary CHW supply temp fix taking hold plant-wide. STILL OPEN: B28 AHU-8 Warehouse (+16.2F, low priority per Zaal), B28 AHU-6 (+4.6F, improved but not resolved), B53 AHU-3 comm fault persists (unchanged). NEW CONCERN: B3 AHU-1 got WORSE (+4.6F -> +6.7F) - moving wrong direction, needs a look. NOTE: cluster of units running 3-7F BELOW setpoint (B51 PIV pair, B12 AHU-1, B30 pair, B56 pair, B3 AHU-2) - not urgent but worth confirming intentional vs drift.

outcome: Pending - need to locate 2552 VAV/VMA zone controller in Metasys (B53 SNE-02, reheat off 1053007CGE Heat Exchanger, same trunk as 2533/2535/2535a VMAs). action: Raised Zone Temperature Setpoint from 72F to 75F on 1053034CGE Rm 2552 (VAV/reheat box) per Tracy McGarr request via Wayne Cameron
outcome: Pending verification. Context: zone was already AT the 72F setpoint per sensor - discharge temp was only 60.3F at 280cfm, likely a draft/mixing issue rather than setpoint deficiency. Reheat valve was at 52% cmd / 0% effort (headroom available). Airflow near a low floor (280 of 3200 rated cfm, likely lab ACH minimum) - raising setpoint should add reheat without changing airflow. Watch Supply Air Flow after change to confirm it does not climb - if it does, box modulates volume with heat demand too.

action: Change confirmed applied: Zone Temperature Setpoint raised 72F -> 75F on 1053034CGE Rm 2552

action: WO #400161 - Metasys changes: CLGOCC-SP lowered 74F->70F (effective cooling SP clamped to 72F by min deadband above 70F heating SP, normal behavior). CLG-MAXFLOW raised 50cfm->100cfm (was equal to CLG-MINFLOW, box had zero cooling modulation range before this).
outcome: ZNT-STATE flipped from Satisfied to Prmy Clg - box now recognizes cooling need. CLG-O/SA-F had not ramped up yet as of last check (zone only 0.8F over effective SP). Going on-site with temp gun to verify discharge air temp at diffuser, duct temp upstream, and radiant panel surface temp before confirming fix.

action: Field verification with temp gun: 67.5F at diffuser (vs 66.4F BAS discharge sensor), 72.6F at thermostat (vs 73.6F BAS zone sensor).
outcome: Both within ~1F of BAS readings - sensors confirmed accurate, no fault. ~5F spread between discharge and room air confirms box is delivering real cooling now (was doing nothing before the CLG-MAXFLOW fix). Zone not yet at Ed requested 68-70F but trending down. Airflow was still ramping toward new 100cfm ceiling at last check - recheck in 20-30 min.

action: RESOLVED - full fix summary for WO #400161. Root causes found: (1) Zone Temperature sensor had a +2F calibration offset applied, so BAS control logic was working off a reading 2F hotter than true room temp the entire time. Corrected offset to 0. (2) CLG-MAXFLOW was equal to CLG-MINFLOW at 50cfm - box had zero cooling modulation range regardless of setpoint. Raised to 100cfm. (3) CLGOCC-SP lowered 74F->70F (effective cooling SP clamped to 72F by min deadband above 70F heating SP).
outcome: Confirmed with door closed that zone temp drops as expected - system now delivering full physical cooling capacity (100cfm, corrected sensor, corrected setpoint). Temp gun verified sensors accurate (~1F match). This explains why local thermostat adjustments never worked for Ed/prior occupant - skewed sensor input plus zero flow range meant no amount of dial-turning could change anything. Ready to close WO #400161 pending final settle check with Ed.

action: Diagnostic test: forced Damper Output to 100% via Operator Override, raised CLG-MAXFLOW to 200cfm, door closed.
outcome: Zone Temperature dropped to 71.8F, actual SA-F hit 338cfm - confirms box/duct can physically deliver far more than the 50cfm it was originally capped at. Real cooling capacity confirmed. REMINDER: release the Damper Output operator override before leaving - it is a manual test override, leaving it in place will overcool/waste energy since it bypasses normal modulation. Let it run under normal control with CLG-MAXFLOW=200cfm and recheck settling temp.

action: Reverted CLG-MAXFLOW back to 50cfm (was testing 100/200cfm). Keeping WO #400161 open for a day.
outcome: Decided to isolate variables - fix the +2F sensor offset first and confirm that alone resolves Ed comfort complaint before committing to a permanent flow cap change. Suspected 50cfm min=max may be intentionally low or may need raising, but not changing it yet. WO comment: recalibrated zone sensor, corrected 2F offset, keeping open a day to confirm.

action: WO #400184 - physical replacement of the OAT sensor that caused the 7/1-7/2 cooling lockout (was reading -39.5F). Unit is Veris HD1NVSTA1 duct RH/Temp transmitter, outdoor/wet-location rated.
outcome: Checking whether only the replaceable probe head needs swapping (pigtail connector, separate from transmitter body) vs full transmitter replacement - open probe circuit is the classic cause of a wildly out-of-range negative reading like we saw. Noting existing wire color landed (5V vs 10V output set: Yellow/Orange=Temp, Green/Blue=Humidity) before disconnecting so replacement matches controller config. This is the permanent fix superseding the temporary OAT+CHW override from 7/1.

action: WO #400184 - requested Amy order replacement Veris HD1NVSTA1 (whole unit, Kele part page confirmed exact model in stock/orderable) rather than sourcing a separate HS-series probe element.
outcome: Awaiting order/delivery. Temporary OAT+CHW override at NAE-10 stays in place until physical replacement is installed and verified against real outdoor conditions.
